premises.text: Lithium brine resources are abundant but solar-evaporation extraction is too slow, water-intensive, carbon-heavy, and costly to meet battery demand
premises.evidence_span: lithium brine industry lack efficient lithium extraction technology to meet the current demands of exploding battery market

premises.text: Nano-mosaic absorbents selectively extract lithium from brine in about 48 hours into battery-grade product with far less water, cost, and carbon than evaporation
premises.evidence_span: develop nano-mosaic absorbents, which are very similar to a sponge

premises.text: Filter units loaded with the absorbents scale lithium throughput for brine and petrochemical operators
premises.evidence_span: these are our filter units, which are five feet long

premises.text: The same selective extraction approach can extend beyond lithium to other chemicals such as nickel and cobalt
premises.evidence_span: not just limited to lithium extraction, but can be extended to various chemical extraction like nickel and cobalt

value.text: Sustainable, efficient lithium supply for the clean-energy battery market
value.evidence_span: provide sustainable energy technology to the global market

causal_links.evidence_span: we have enough resources of lithium, but lithium brine industry lack efficient lithium extraction technology
extracting lithium within 48 hours and process it into battery grade
extended to various chemical extraction like nickel and cobalt

notes: v1.5.1 process+performance package: 48h timing, water, cost, and zero carbon folded into P2 rather than separate premises. Industry-lacks-efficient-tech kept as the motivating brine-extraction gap (P1) because it is the go-to-market problem the process answers. Revenue-per-filter figures treated as traction.
